accuracy_findings.claim: The system view shows the points next to the owner's name.
accuracy_findings.problem: The points marker also shows on autonomous systems, which have no owner. Their owner block reads "Not claimed" / "Autonomous system" instead of a name. The sentence is still true for owned systems and dominions, just a bit narrow.
accuracy_findings.evidence: front/src/game/components/galaxy/system/Properties.vue:38-56. The marker-label v-if is only !['uninhabitable','uninhabited'].includes(system.status), so it renders for inhabited_neutral too, and there the owner block shows galaxy.system.properties.not_claimed / autonomous_system (lines 62-65).
accuracy_findings.fix: Optionally reword to "The system view shows the points next to the owner block" or "at the top of the system's properties".

votes.reason: The table and bullets lay out the class tiers and scoring clearly, but two unexplained terms make a first-week player pause.
stumbles: "not the rounded one" — the page never shows or explains a "rounded" population value to contrast with the exact one
"Path of Influence" is bolded as if a defined game term but nothing on this page says what it is

votes.reason: The table gives exact population breakpoints and point values, and the bullets clarify the inclusive-threshold rule and what the points feed into, so a skimming player gets the rule in one read with only a small naming hiccup.
stumbles: Column header "Star System Points" is never used again in the prose — later bullets just say "points" ("worth the points in the last column", "System points mode"), so it takes a beat to confirm these are the same number.

"From population" doesn't say inclusive vs exclusive by itself; you have to read down to "A system just short of a class's population stays in the class below" to confirm 40 itself counts as Minor Colony, not Outpost.

No unit or scale is given for the population numbers (40, 60, 70...) on this page itself — a player has to already know or follow the population link to know what these figures mean in absolute terms.
